sections.heading: C — License loss, seat belts and impaired driving
sections.markdown:
## C — License loss, seat belts and impaired driving

FACT_ID: sec02-F01 | anchor: A01
Failing to pay court-ordered child support is another way to lose your Colorado driving privilege. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec02-F02 | anchor: A01
You must carry proof of insurance whenever you drive, and failing to show valid evidence of insurance when an officer asks can cost you your license. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec02-F03 | anchor: A01
A conviction for buying or possessing alcohol while under 21 can also lead to losing your driving privilege. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec02-F04 | anchor: A01
On public roads, Colorado requires a fastened seat belt in every vehicle with factory-installed belts for the driver, every front-seat passenger, and every child under 16. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec02-F05 | anchor: A01
The only seat belt exceptions are emergency personnel, passenger and school buses, farm equipment, delivery-van drivers while working, and anyone carrying a physician statement saying they cannot wear a belt for physical or psychological reasons. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec02-F06 | anchor: A01
When no parent is in the vehicle, the driver is responsible for making sure each child is properly secured in the correct child restraint. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec02-F07 | anchor: A01
A child younger than 2 who weighs less than 40 pounds must ride in a rear-facing child restraint in the back seat. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec02-F08 | anchor: A01
A child younger than 2 who weighs 40 pounds or more may ride in either a rear-facing or a forward-facing child restraint. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec02-F09 | anchor: A01
A child aged 2 to under 4 who weighs at least 20 pounds must ride in a rear-facing or forward-facing child restraint, in the back seat when one is available. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec02-F10 | anchor: A01
A child aged 4 to under 9 who weighs at least 40 pounds must use a child restraint or booster seat in the back seat when the vehicle has one. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec02-F11 | anchor: A01
Children from 9 to 18 must be restrained by a seat belt or a child restraint used as the manufacturer directs. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec02-F12 | anchor: A01
When the driver is under 18, every passenger must be belted or properly restrained, and the passenger count may never be more than the number of seat belts. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec02-F13 | anchor: A01
Impaired driving by alcohol, drugs or a mix of them is among the leading causes of crashes and deaths on the road. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec02-F14 | anchor: A01
Alcohol is a depressant: it slows brain function, reflexes and reaction time, harms thinking and coordination, and makes risky moves such as speeding or abrupt turns more likely. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec02-F15 | anchor: A01
It is illegal to have an open container of alcohol or of marijuana in the passenger area of a vehicle on a public road. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec02-F16 | anchor: A01
DWAI, Driving While Ability Impaired, means impairment to even the slightest degree, while DUI, Driving Under the Influence, means being substantially incapable of driving safely. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec02-F17 | anchor: A01
An impaired driving conviction does not rest on BAC alone; it can be proven by driving behavior, the officer observations during the stop, and performance on Standardized Field Sobriety Tests. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec02-F18 | anchor: A01
A driver can be convicted of DUI per se when BAC is greater than 0.08%. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec02-F19 | anchor: A01
Your license may be revoked for refusing a chemical test, for a BAC over .08, for a BAC over .02 if you are under 21, or over .04 if you are a CDL driver. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec02-F20 | anchor: A01
BAC depends on how much you drank, your body weight, how fast you drank, how long since the last drink, and your sex, so two people drinking the same amount can differ. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec02-F21 | anchor: A01
Beer, wine and liquor are equally intoxicating per standard drink: 12 ounces of beer, 5 ounces of wine and 1.5 ounces of distilled spirits each hold about the same alcohol. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec02-F22 | anchor: A01
Only time sobers you up, and on average BAC falls by about 0.015% per hour. [A01]
Why it matters: Coffee, showers and fresh air do not lower BAC.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec02-F23 | anchor: A02
A first DWAI conviction for a driver 21 or older is tied to a 0.05% BAC level and carries 8 points, a fine of $200 to $500, 2 to 180 days in jail and 24 to 48 hours of public service. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec02-F24 | anchor: A02
A first DUI for a driver 21 or older is tied to 0.08% BAC and brings a 9-month revocation, a fine of $600 to $1,000, 5 to 365 days in jail and 48 to 96 hours of public service. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec02-F25 | anchor: A02
A second DWAI or DUI brings a 1-year revocation, a fine of $600 to $1,500, 10 to 365 days in jail and 48 to 120 hours of public service. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec02-F26 | anchor: A02
A third or later DWAI or DUI brings a 2-year revocation, a fine of $600 to $1,500, 60 to 365 days in jail and 48 to 120 hours of public service. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec02-F27 | anchor: A02
A driver under 21 convicted of DUI or DWAI faces revocation on a first conviction if they do not finish the court-ordered evaluation or program, and a second or third conviction means mandatory revocation. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec02-F28 | anchor: A02
Anyone under 21 convicted of buying or possessing alcohol can have their driving privilege revoked even when no driving was involved. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec02-F29 | anchor: A02
Driving impaired by any drug, whether illegal drugs, marijuana, prescription or over-the-counter medicine, is illegal and carries the same penalties as alcohol-impaired driving. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec02-F30 | anchor: A02
Using marijuana or another drug for medical reasons is no defense to a DUI or DWAI charge. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec02-F31 | anchor: A02
Drug impairment depends on the dose and the person; tranquilizers, pain killers and allergy or cold remedies can all impair driving. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec02-F32 | anchor: A02
Read medication labels for warnings before you drive, and ask your doctor or pharmacist when a label is missing or unclear. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0007]
